## Common model

The AR(1) mean-change model is

$$X_t=\mu_t+\rho(X_{t-1}-\mu_{t-1})+\varepsilon_t,
\qquad \varepsilon_t\stackrel{iid}{\sim}N(0,\sigma^2),$$

with $|\rho|<1$ and piecewise-constant $\mu_t$. For a change after $\tau$,
the transition residual is

$$X_{\tau+1}-\rho X_\tau-\mu_2+\rho\mu_1,$$

which must be included in an exact likelihood calculation.

## SVP criterion

For each candidate segment $I=[s,t]$, a validity test decides whether it is
admissible. SVP minimizes lexicographically

$$\left(K(\mathcal P),\;\sum_{I\in\mathcal P}C(I)\right),$$

over valid partitions: first the number of segments, then the total cost.

## Exact fixed-variance test: `AR1`

`AR1` scans every possible change-point using the exact fixed-$\rho$ Gaussian
log-likelihood ratio. Prefix sums make each candidate calculation constant time
after updating sufficient statistics. Use it when `rho` and `sigma2` are known.

```r
SVP(y, gamma=8, test="AR1", rho=.7, sigma2=1)
```

## Profiled exact test: `AR1Profile`

`AR1Profile` uses the same transition-corrected likelihood but profiles out
the innovation variance. Its statistic is based on

$$T=\frac{m}{2}\log(RSS_0/RSS_1),$$

where $m$ is the number of usable AR transitions. Its threshold calibration
is different from the fixed-variance test.

```r
SVP(y, gamma=8, test="AR1Profile", rho=.7, profile_sigma=TRUE)
```

## Fast innovation/FOCuS test: `AR1Focus`

`AR1Focus` applies Gaussian FOCuS to the innovations

$$Z_t=X_t-\rho X_{t-1}.$$

It updates candidate likelihood states online and prunes candidates. It is
fast and suitable for streaming data, but is an innovation-based method and
need not return the exact likelihood partition.

```r
SVP(y, gamma=8, test="AR1Focus", rho=.7, sigma2=1)
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `y`/`data` | Observed numeric series. |
| `gamma` | Validity threshold; larger values accept more segments. |
| `test` | `AR1`, `AR1Profile`, or `AR1Focus`. |
| `rho` | Fixed AR coefficient, strictly between -1 and 1. |
| `sigma2` | Innovation variance for fixed-variance tests. |
| `profile_sigma` | Profile the innovation variance. |
| `prune_after_if_unvalid` | Permanently remove starts after invalid extensions when stability is justified. |
| `prune_before_if_invalid` | Remove earlier starts at the current endpoint when inverse stability is justified. |
| `quantile` | Quantile used for robust nuisance-parameter estimation. |

Estimate an unknown AR coefficient with `AR1_rho(y)` and pass the same estimate
to every method in a comparison. The script
`compare_ar1_svp.R` reports partitions and runtimes without writing figures.
